Overall AEs were reported in 1,640 participants (26.2%) and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in 1,610 participants (25.8%). Serious AEs occurred in 2 participants (<0.1%), and serious ADRs in 1 participant (<0.1%); no unexpected serious ADRs were identified.

### Stakeholder perspectives on implementing geographic information systems for leprosy elimination in Pakistan: A qualitative study.
Published Nov 5, 2026 · Retrieved Nov 9, 2026
By highlighting elevated risk areas, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) are a cost-effective solution to improve leprosy case detection by guiding targeted interventions to high-risk areas. Barriers included the limited local capacity in complex GIS data analysis, hybrid digital-manual workflows, historical data lacking GPS, and ensuring feedback and ownership for staff members. This study's purpose was to investigate the perceived GIS implementation facilitators and barriers, to support targeted interventions and advance the Zero Leprosy strategy.

Published Nov 3, 2026 · Retrieved Nov 9, 2026
These include cultural factors such as context-blind universalism and organizational environments that discourage public-sector entrepreneurship, as well as organizational design features such as fragmented data systems, a lack of incentives to pursue a public health career, and rigid performance-based budgeting. The study proposes that improving the government's capacity to respond to health threats requires integrating whole-of-government principles into existing NPM arrangements to strengthen both hierarchical and horizontal coordination. To address infectious diseases such as dengue, the World Health organization advocates a 'whole-of-government' approach that promotes coordination across all levels of government within the health sector and across related sectors.
